edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The Buyer shall pay the Seller the purchase price set forth on Schedule 1 (the “Purchase Price”), subject to the adjustments, if any, specified in Schedule 1. The Purchase Price shall be paid at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Seller at least three Business Days before Closing.
edits.name: Purchase Price

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, or at such other time as the parties agree in writing, subject to satisfaction or waiver by the Buyer of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement. The Buyer’s obligation to close is conditioned on the Seller’s representations and warranties being true and correct in all material respects as of Closing, the Seller having performed in all material respects its obligations due at or before Closing, and the absence of any order prohibiting the transaction.
edits.name: Closing

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents and warrants that the financial statements delivered to the Buyer were prepared in accordance with consistently applied accounting principles and fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Seller as of the dates and for the periods indicated. The Seller further represents and warrants that, except as disclosed in writing to the Buyer, the Seller has no liabilities required to be reflected or reserved against in those financial statements other than liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business since the date of the most recent financial statements.
edits.name: Representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. The Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer and its affiliates and their respective representatives from and against all losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) arising out of or resulting from any breach of the Seller’s representations, warranties, covenants, or agreements in this Agreement, or any undisclosed liability of the Seller. The indemnification obligations shall survive Closing for the period specified in this Agreement; claims made by written notice before expiration shall survive until resolved. The parties shall set out in this Agreement any applicable baskets, caps, and procedures for asserting and resolving indemnification claims.
edits.name: Indemnity

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE; CLOSING ADJUSTMENT. The indicative purchase price is USD 16,250,000 (the “Purchase Price”), subject to the adjustments in this Section. The parties shall agree in writing before signing on a normalized target level of Net Working Capital (the “Target Working Capital”), determined using the accounting principles and practices consistently applied in preparing the Seller’s most recent annual financial statements, with illustrative calculations to be included on Schedule 1. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price, (a) plus the amount, if any, by which Closing Net Working Capital exceeds Target Working Capital, or minus the amount, if any, by which Closing Net Working Capital is below Target Working Capital, (b) plus Closing Cash, and (c) minus Closing Indebtedness and unpaid Seller Transaction Expenses (the resulting amount, the “Estimated Closing Payment”). “Closing Net Working Capital” means current assets, excluding Cash and income tax assets, less current liabilities, excluding Indebtedness, income tax liabilities, and Seller Transaction Expenses, in each case calculated in accordance with the agreed principles on Schedule 1. “Indebtedness” means borrowed money, accrued interest thereon, and obligations in the nature of borrowed money, including finance leases, but excluding trade payables incurred in the ordinary course and included in Closing Net Working Capital. At least three Business Days before Closing, the Seller shall deliver its good-faith estimate of Closing Net Working Capital, Closing Cash, Closing Indebtedness, and Seller Transaction Expenses, with reasonable supporting detail. The Estimated Closing Payment shall be paid at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated in writing by the Seller at least three Business Days before Closing. Within 60 days after Closing, the Buyer shall deliver a closing statement setting forth its calculation of those items and the final purchase price. The Seller shall have 30 days to review the statement and supporting records and deliver a written notice of any disputed items, stating the basis and amount of each dispute. Undisputed items shall be final. The parties shall attempt in good faith to resolve disputed items for 20 days, after which unresolved items shall be submitted to an independent nationally recognized accounting firm mutually selected by the parties, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator, whose determination shall be limited to the disputed items and within the range of the parties’ positions. The firm’s fees shall be allocated in proportion to the extent each party does not prevail. The final purchase price shall be paid, as applicable, by the Buyer or Seller within five Business Days after final determination. The closing statement and review process shall provide reasonable access to relevant books and records, subject to customary confidentiality protections. The parties shall cooperate in good faith to complete Schedule 1, including the Target Working Capital and illustrative calculation, before signing.
edits.name: Section 1

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. (a) Subject to the limitations in this Section, the Seller shall indemnify and hold harmless the Buyer and its affiliates and their respective representatives from and against Losses to the extent arising from (i) any breach of a representation or warranty made by the Seller in this Agreement or (ii) any breach of a covenant or agreement of the Seller in this Agreement. “Losses” means actual losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees), but excludes punitive, exemplary, and consequential damages, except to the extent actually awarded to a third party or arising from fraud. The Seller shall have no indemnification obligation merely because a liability was not disclosed, except to the extent that the liability results in a breach of a representation or warranty or covenant expressly set forth in this Agreement. (b) A claim for breach of a representation or warranty must be made by written notice describing in reasonable detail the basis for the claim and, to the extent then reasonably practicable, the estimated amount, before the applicable survival period expires. General representations and warranties shall survive for 18 months after Closing; claims properly noticed before expiration shall survive until resolved. Claims for breach of fundamental representations concerning organization, authority, due authorization, and title to the shares shall survive until 60 days after expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms, or, if no period is specified, for 18 months after Closing. Claims based on fraud shall survive as provided by applicable law. (c) The Seller shall have no liability for claims under Section 4(a)(i) unless aggregate Losses exceed USD 150,000, in which case the Seller shall be liable for all such Losses from the first dollar. The Seller’s aggregate liability for claims under Section 4(a)(i), other than claims for breach of fundamental representations, shall not exceed 20% of the Purchase Price. Aggregate liability for breach of fundamental representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price. The basket and caps do not apply to fraud or to claims under Section 4(a)(ii) for breach of covenants, which shall be subject to the applicable survival period and shall not exceed the Purchase Price in the aggregate, except in the case of fraud. (d) The Buyer shall give the Seller prompt written notice of any claim, provided that failure to give prompt notice shall relieve the Seller only to the extent materially prejudiced. The Seller may, by written notice, assume control of the defense of a third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Buyer, provided the claim seeks monetary damages only and does not involve a material ongoing business relationship or equitable relief. The Buyer may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. The Seller may not settle a claim without the Buyer’s written consent if the settlement includes an admission of wrongdoing, imposes non-monetary relief, or does not provide an unconditional release of the Buyer and its affiliates. If the Seller does not timely assume the defense, the Buyer may defend and settle the claim in a commercially reasonable manner, subject to the Seller’s indemnification obligations. The parties shall reasonably cooperate in the defense of any claim. (e) The Buyer shall not recover more than once for the same Loss, and any indemnifiable Loss shall be reduced by insurance proceeds and other third-party recoveries actually received, net of reasonable collection costs and premium increases. No provision of this Section limits liability for fraud.
edits.name: Section 4
